sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 607.5 ± 58.9 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Ca²⁺ imaging with 100 µM UTP: marked intracellular Ca²⁺ increase, kinetics similar to wild-type P2Y4-transfected cells; surface display confirmed by immunofluorescence showing cytoplasmic and membrane localisation.
sites.rationale: P2Y4 has no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–35 as extracellular, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus available for a prepend tag. The 5′-terminus Myc construct is therefore unambiguously insert_after_residue=0, with residue_after=M (residue 1). L2 and L3 confirm both surface display and preserved Gq/Ca²⁺ signalling, giving the highest validation level. Human P2Y4 cDNA cloned into pCS2 with Myc epitope tags at the 5′ terminus, transiently transfected into SH-SY5Y cells. Immunofluorescence confirmed membrane localisation (L2); 100 µM UTP stimulation produced a marked Ca²⁺ increase with kinetics similar to untagged P2Y4 (L3).

sources.claim: Moreover, by the use of polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with Platinum Pfx polymerase (Invitrogen, Paisley, UK), human P2Y 4 cDNA was amplified with oligonucleotides containing EcoRI and XhoI restriction sequences for the subcloning into a pCS2 plasmid containing myc epitope tags (EQKLISEEDL) at the 5′ terminus.

literature_notes: L4/L5/L6 describe a pEGFPN1 C-terminal GFP fusion to P2Y4. The pEGFPN1 vector places GFP at the protein C-terminus (after residue 365). The topology landmarks assign residues 310–365 to the intracellular compartment, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface tag site; it is recorded in other_positions. L6 also notes that the N178T natural variant (ECL2, residue 178) shows reduced GFP fluorescence relative to WT, but this is expression-level data for a missense variant, not a tag-insertion experiment at that residue, so it does not qualify as a ledger-supported insertion site.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP fusion (pEGFPN1) expressed in HEK-293 cells; C-terminus (310–365) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
